summary.headline: Anupam Rasayan Q2 FY27 consolidated EBITDA rose 41% YoY to INR202 crores at ~25% margin, helped by Bliss GVS acquisition completion.
summary.overview: Consolidated total income for Q2 FY27 was INR821 crores, up 11% YoY, with EBITDA of INR202 crores (about 25% margin vs 19.4%) and PAT of INR65 crores (up 14%). H1 FY27 total income was INR1,489 crores (up 21%), EBITDA INR377 crores (25.5% margin) and PAT INR116 crores (up 10%). Bliss GVS Pharma was acquired on September 28, 2026 (about 50.07% stake), so it contributed only three days to Q2 results. Standalone revenue fell YoY because Q2 FY26 included a one-time sale of about INR180 crores. Management guided H2 FY27 consolidated revenue of INR2,400-2,500 crores.

segments.name: Life science specialty chemicals
segments.commentary: Contributed 42% of Q2 FY27 revenue and 41% of H1 FY27 revenue. Pharma KSMs make up about 20-25% of group revenue per management.

segments.name: Performance Materials
segments.commentary: Contributed 28% of Q2 FY27 and 29% of H1 FY27 revenue; management cited higher contribution from this segment as a key driver of margin improvement.

segments.name: Other fluorinated products
segments.commentary: Contributed 29% of Q2 FY27 and 28% of H1 FY27 revenue. Polymers account for about 20-25% of revenue per management.

segments.name: Bliss GVS Pharma (acquired)
segments.commentary: Consolidated only from September 28, 2026 (three days in Q2). Management guides a 22-24% consolidated EBITDA margin for Bliss, with utilisation in the 40s%.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 consolidated revenue guided at INR2,400-2,500 crores, annualising to INR4,800-5,000 crores.
Organic growth of 20-25% expected over the near-term three to five years.
Consolidated EBITDA margin guidance of 22-24% retained; management declined to raise guidance despite 25% Q2 and 34% standalone margin.
Revenue cyclicality expected to reduce over the next four to eight quarters as Pharma and Performance Materials grow.
Synergies from Bliss expected to show benefit in three to four quarters.
Six-year US metal contract expected to contribute INR100-150 crores this year, with run rate roughly doubling over the next one to one-and-half years.
Standalone order book (about INR17,000 crores) implies roughly INR2,500 crores average annual revenue; FY27 expected at 1.8x-2x the prior year's roughly INR350 crores from this contract.
capex_capacity: Bliss GVS capacity utilisation in the 40s%, with growth ongoing per management.
Multipurpose plants and pre-built capacity allowed commercialisation of the US metal product in four months; supplies began November 2026.
Elementium contract discussions ongoing; monthly supplies have started on schedule.
Jayhawk provides US manufacturing presence; Anupam holds 100% of Jayhawk per management.
demand_pricing: Cumulative LOIs and long-term contracts about INR17,496 crores, providing multi-year visibility.
Six-year long-term supply agreement signed in Q2 FY27 with a US-based global specialty metal manufacturer, entering a new geological resources segment.
Management cited higher-margin product sales and pass-through of price increases as drivers of margin; standalone EBITDA margin around 34% in the quarter.
Japanese customer volume potentially tripling with Jayhawk-sourced material, per management.
Bliss CDMO conversations described as active, but no quantification shared.

qa_highlights.question: Progress on acquiring API assets to complement Bliss's formulations business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said alternatives are being evaluated and conversations continue; nothing to share publicly yet, but the company is actively looking.

qa_highlights.question: Steady-state EBITDA margin for Bliss?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided 22-24%, the same as the consolidated group average, and said it would be cautious despite Bliss's better H1 margin (about 26.2%).

qa_highlights.question: Funding structure of the Bliss acquisition, debt terms and Elementium LOI progress?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR1,450 crores is quasi-equity (buy-out right over a long timeframe) and about INR300 crores is debt at the subsidiary level priced in single digits with no servicing pressure in year one. Elementium contract talks are ongoing with supplies started monthly.

qa_highlights.question: What numbers to expect in coming quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: H2 FY27 consolidated revenue of INR2,400-2,500 crores, annualising to INR4,800-5,000 crores, with 20-25% organic growth over three to five years.

qa_highlights.question: Is there seasonality in Bliss's business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment as Bliss is a separately listed entity; it will urge Bliss to hold calls.

qa_highlights.question: Jayhawk EBITDA margin improvement initiatives?
qa_highlights.answer: Three immediate levers: process optimisation (solvents, acids, raw materials), sourcing from India via Anupam, and reducing effluent treatment costs.

risks_watch: Q2 standalone revenue decline versus a one-time INR180 crore sale in Q2 FY26; underlying run rate is not clearly disclosed.
Bliss GVS contributed only three days in Q2; H2 consolidation and Bliss's margin will drive reported numbers.
Quasi-equity INR1,450 crore instrument from Bain Capital-led investors carries buy-out rights; future obligations are unclear.
Working capital cycle still at 271 days (ex-Bliss); cash of about INR750 crores held across entities for working capital.
Management said it would not raise margin guidance despite a 34% standalone margin quarter; margin sustainability is unproven.
Limited disclosure from Bliss (CDMO pipeline, 62 molecules, approvals, seasonality) because it is separately listed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on strategy, growth and order visibility, but cautious and evasive on specifics: management repeatedly declined to quantify CDMO pipeline, Bliss seasonality and margin upside, and held guidance at 22-24% EBITDA.
key_quotes: Our consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 25% in Q2 FY27 compared to 19% in the corresponding quarter last year, while H1 margins improved from 26% from 22%.
I would urge to caution and continue to guide at the numbers that we have been guiding.
Our business is not to profit from the price volatility of the raw materials or otherwise.

growth.why: Management guided H2 FY27 consolidated revenue of INR2,400-2,500 crore (annualising to INR4,800-5,000 crore) and 20-25% organic growth over 3-5 years, backed by cumulative LOIs and long-term contracts of about INR17,496 crore and a six-year US metal contract expected to add INR100-150 crore this year, but no new plant capacity was quantified and the H2 guide is not reconciled to specific capacity

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin was ~25% vs 19.4% and H1 was 25.5% vs 22.2%, driven by higher-margin Performance Materials and price pass-through, but management held consolidated guidance at 22-24% and called the 34% standalone quarter unproven.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Bliss GVS utilisation is in the 40s% so its existing capacity has headroom, and the US metal product was commercialised in four months using multipurpose and pre-built capacity; no new plant or line was quantified.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guided H2 FY27 consolidated revenue of INR2,400-2,500 crore (annualising to INR4,800-5,000 crore), supported by INR17,496 crore of LOIs and long-term contracts and a six-year US metal contract adding INR100-150 crore this year.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed; utilisation is only given for Bliss (40s%), which is low, so no new capex announcement is implied.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to raise the 22-24% EBITDA margin guidance despite a 25% Q2 margin and 34% standalone margin, so the guidance is being held rather than raised.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Bliss contributed only three days in Q2, its margin of 22-24% is untested, and the 271-day working capital cycle and the INR1,450 crore quasi-equity obligation add risk to H2 delivery.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: The US metal product began supplies in November 2026 and Elementium monthly supplies have started, while Bliss CDMO conversations are active but unquantified.

rows.label: Six-year US metal contract ramp
rows.why: Contract expected to add INR100-150 crore this year, with run rate roughly doubling over the next one to one-and-half years from about INR350 crore prior-year base.

rows.label: Japanese customer volume tripling via Jayhawk
rows.why: Management said Japanese customer volume could potentially triple with Jayhawk-sourced material, but no quantification or timeline was given.

rows.label: Bliss synergies and Jayhawk margin levers
rows.why: Management expects Bliss synergies to show benefit in three to four quarters, and has named three Jayhawk levers: process optimisation, India sourcing and lower effluent costs.

tone.note: Management was confident on order visibility, the US metal contract and H2 revenue guide of INR2,400-2,500 crore, but cautious and evasive on Bliss margins, seasonality, CDMO pipeline and API acquisition, and held margin guidance at 22-24%; analysts pressed on the sustainability of the 34% standalon
